headline.text: Management wording (confident vs cautious cues, -1..+1): prepared +1.00, qa +0.12

tone.method: lexical cue counts on management sentences; indicative of wording, not a measure of business health

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Starting with the top line, adjusted sales were $24.7 billion, up 16% organically, including double-digit commercial aftermarket and defense growth.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Adjusted EPS of $1.89 was up 21% year-over-year, driven by 18% growth in segment operating profit, and free cash flow was strong at $2.9 billion.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Our backlog stands at yet another record of $289 billion, up 22% year-over-year and 6% sequentially.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: On the commercial side of the business, demand also remained strong as evidenced by our continued growth.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Notably, at Pratt, AirAsia placed an order for 150 A220 aircraft, which are exclusively powered by GTF engines, adding a new GTF operator and further expanding our installed base in a key growth region.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And Collins signed a new 5-year agreement with Air New Zealand to provide MRO services for engine nacelles on their full fleet of 787 aircraft.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So overall, a very strong quarter that builds on our momentum from Q1.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: For the year, global RPKs are expected to grow in all regions outside of the Middle East and engine retirements have remained relatively low, both factors that support our outlook for strong commercial aftermarket growth this year.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Airframers also continue to cite strong demand with further rate growth expected in the second half of the year, driving the need for our OE products across narrow-body, wide-body and business jet platforms.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: On the international front, the need for integrated air and missile defense systems remains very strong.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So based on our first half execution and the demand strength we're seeing across our commercial and defense markets, we're raising our full year outlook for adjusted sales, EPS and free cash flow.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Additionally, our Coyote counter-UAS effector, which has been deployed by both the U.S. Army and Navy, has been incredibly effective in the field and is in high demand.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Next is innovation for future growth.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We continue to make focused investments to meet long-term global demand faster, including increasing capacity across RTX.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: For example, Raytheon is investing an additional $100 million domestically to increase GEM-T component production and accelerate LTAMDS's test capabilities to meet the growing global need for this 360-degree sensor.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Just this month, Raytheon announced a collaboration with multiple NATO nations to identify additional European suppliers for AMRAAM components to accelerate deliveries of this critical munition.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: On the commercial side, Pratt announced additional investments of more than $100 million in the U.S. to expand GTF MRO capacity across multiple sites in Texas, Florida and Arkansas.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: These investments will support new automation and repair capabilities to increase shop throughput.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And at Collins, we continue to expand our footprint in growth regions.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Collins was down-selected to deliver their mission autonomy software for the U.S. Air Force's collaborative combat aircraft program.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: This type of autonomy will be critical in next-generation fighter development to maximize manned and unmanned teaming.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Pratt received aircraft certification for the GTF Advantage engine and started its deliveries to Airbus.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: As a reminder, the Advantage will double the time on wing performance and is fully interchangeable with current GTF fleet.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And at Raytheon, the team is utilizing a modified TJ150 engine from Pratt to develop a new longer-range variant of our precision-guided air-launched Stormbreaker effector.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: This cross-company initiative has moved from concept to an upcoming flight test in less than 12 months to support delivering this new capability.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So overall, we continue to make good progress across our strategic priorities as we execute and innovate for our customers.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: In the second quarter, adjusted sales of $24.7 billion were up 14% on an adjusted basis and 16% organically year-over-year.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: This strong organic growth was driven by all three channels with commercial OE up 9%, commercial aftermarket up 18% and defense up 16%.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: Adjusted segment operating profit of $3.2 billion was up 18% year-over-year, primarily driven by the drop-through on higher volume.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: Adjusted earnings per share of $1.89 was up 21% from the prior year, driven by the strong segment operating profit growth I just mentioned.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: On a GAAP basis, earnings per share from continuing operations was $1.57 and included $0.27 of acquisition accounting adjustments and $0.05 of restructuring and all other nonrecurring items.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So overall, I'm pleased with our strong financial performance through the first half of the year and our continued execution across the business.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: As Chris said upfront, we are updating our full year outlook based on our first half performance and our strong backlog position.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: On the top line, we're raising our full year adjusted sales outlook by $2.5 billion to a new range of $95 billion to $96 billion, up from our prior range of $92.5 billion to $93.5 billion.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: This translates to full year RTX organic sales growth of between 8% and 9%, up from our prior range of between 5% and 6%.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: Breaking this down further, we now expect commercial OE sales to grow mid- to high single digits, up from the prior expectation of mid-single digits, primarily attributable to the production ramp at Collins.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: Within commercial aftermarket, we now expect sales to grow low double digits across the company this year, up from our prior expectation of high single digits, driven by the strength at Pratt that I mentioned earlier.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And with respect to defense sales, we now see growth of high single digits, which is at the higher end of our prior range of mid- to high single digits.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: On the bottom line, we're increasing our outlook for adjusted earnings per share by $0.40 on the low end and $0.35 on the high end.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: At the midpoint of our updated outlook, this increase is driven by approximately $0.26 of higher segment operating profit, principally from the net drop-through on the higher volume across the segments as well as favorable defense mix and improved productivity, primarily at Raytheon.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: Finally, we now expect free cash flow to be between $8.5 billion and $8.75 billion for the full year, up from our prior range of $8.25 billion to $8.75 billion, primarily driven by higher segment operating profit.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We drove very strong financial performance in the first half of the year and are confident in our updated full year outlook.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And I want to thank the entire RTX team for their commitment to our mission.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We have strong conviction in the long-term demand across our commercial and defense markets, and we believe that RTX is exceptionally well positioned with leading franchises, a growing installed base, a record backlog and the scale to invest in capacity and technology.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Our focus will remain on executing and innovating for our customers to drive continued organic sales growth, margin expansion and robust free cash flow this year and well into the future.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: I think like many of us, we're pleased to see that the U.S. base budget request crossing the $1 trillion mark, that's significant.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And this, plus the multiyear requests that are in there show the continued demand, I think, for years to come, a really strong demand signal.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So significant engagement with the supply chain, making sure they understand what they're going to need to do, what our volumes are going to look like, what capacity we're going to need, what investments we and they are going to need to make.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And we're making some of those investments today.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: Also engaging with second and third potential suppliers where we have sole-source positions where, frankly, we need to increase the competition and increase the capacity.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We'll see how the budget ultimately shakes out.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: Obviously, really pleased with the first half performance of cash flow.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: The first is, you'll recall, last year, in the second quarter, Pratt was undergoing a 4-week work stoppage that delayed some engine deliveries that, therefore, delayed cash collections.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So we feel good about the second half, but a little bit of timing there between what we had penciled in for Q3 versus Q2.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: As far as the outlook, we took the bottom end of the range up $250 million to reflect the higher segment operating profit that we're putting through in our guidance updates today.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: That's offset a little bit by some working capital headwinds.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So when we started the year, we thought we'd see a slight tailwind from working capital as we sit here today, given we've added 3 points of organic growth to our outlook for the year, we're going to be building a little bit of inventory to make sure that we're prepared to deliver the continued ramp, not only in the second half of the year, but the growth that we see coming through in early 2027.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: Again, feel good where we are, and we'll continue to monitor this as we go through the rest of the year.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: As far as the revenue in the second half, let me kind of share a few thoughts here.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: For the full year, our organic sales are going to be up 8% to 9%.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So very strong growth, like I just said, up 3 points from where we were.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So still growing, still really strong, but again, some unique comparisons.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And then another point I would make about the second half for Pratt on the large commercial engine side, our install engines will continue to grow, but there'll be some lower revenue as the mix shifts more towards installs and away from spares.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And in fact, we now think our OE sales for Pratt will be down in the low single-digit range as we continue to support that really strong material growth on the MRO side, and you saw that in the second quarter numbers.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: On the Raytheon side, also some difficult compares.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: In the first half of last year, sales were up about 4%.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: We had 9% growth in the second half of last year.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And so that's really good for getting product out the door, but it does put a little bit of pressure on the growth rate, which is still fairly robust in the mid-single-digit range in the second half.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So 12% growth in the first half, seeing in that 8%, 9% range in the second half.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And so - and we're also staying fairly prudent on the commercial aftermarket side.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So we haven't changed our outlook there as we continue to monitor the macro situation.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So pleased with that on a unit level.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: The sales decrease was due to mix as again, we continue to ensure that we have strong material flow into our MRO shops.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: As we mentioned, we saw a good decline in GTF AOGs, down 25% in the first half of the year.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We'll be up in the second half of the year there, and we'll deliver a record number of GTF engines this year.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So we still see the margin expansion, not just this year, but we expect that to continue in years thereafter as this aftermarket continues to gain further traction and the profitability continues to accrue to those contracts.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: I would say we're really pleased with the Raytheon performance this year.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: The demand obviously continues to be strong, $20 billion of awards in Q2 and an $86 billion backlog.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And the mix of that demand continues to be pretty favorable.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So all of those things go into what we consider to be Raytheon being on track to continuing to drive margin expansion in its business and getting to that, we'll call it, full potential area that we talked about previously.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So cumulatively, year-to-date, we're about $40 million, which frankly isn't that significant, which tells me that we've got a good solid base margin in the business in the backlog.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: But again, having achieved the 12-plus percent margin here and then as you look at the outlook for the rest of the year, seeing it still in the mid-12% range, we feel really good about the trajectory that we're on.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And all the while, we're able to make investments that we need to do to not just support the new capacity for additional current products, but to invest in new products as well.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: I think our priorities on the capital allocation front continue to be consistent, and that's investing in the business.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: You've heard us talk a lot today in our prepared remarks about the demand and the demand we've talked a lot on the defense side continues to be strong on both the commercial and defense sides of the house.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So continuing to invest in the business to make sure that we've got the right capacity and a healthy supply chain will continue to be a priority.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: A commitment to the dividend, for sure, obviously, we've raised the dividend again here recently.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: On the M&A front, I wouldn't say that anything that's swirling around out there is going to change our thoughts on that.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And we're going to continue to be disciplined around those types of opportunities.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So really no change in our mind about how we think about capital allocation.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And so for us, it's just about driving execution, investing and making sure that we're delivering for our customers and the rest will take care of itself.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So I feel really good about the future of the V2500.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And again, when you get to this particular piece of the life cycle, you start to see things go through a managed decline, and that's exactly what we're doing.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: There's still going to be some strong contribution from those platforms over the next several years, and we will ultimately manage that decline over a period of years.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And so we still see very steady and growing revenues in that portfolio through the end of this decade.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: So I think big picture at Pratt, the size of the GTF fleet and the aftermarket that it is and will generate and continue to grow over the next five, ten years, will offset any of the managed decline on the legacy fleets and then some.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: We remain prudent in the way we look at the booking rates on those, and we're introducing a lot of new material and additional benefits to the GTF engine over the coming couple of years.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: That will grow in the second half, the installs.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And Chris talked about just a few minutes ago that we'll deliver a record number of engines to Airbus this year and ahead of our market share.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: We're pleased by the rate increases that we're seeing on the OE side.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: It doesn't come with profit, but nonetheless, building confidence in the supply chain performance there, and that's enabled us to sort of take up the top line as it relates to those deliveries that we see coming in the second half.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We'll see how the budget ultimately pieces together.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: But the international continues to grow as well.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We have a strong installed base, both in the Middle East and in Europe.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So these are things we're going to continue to leverage as the demand grows.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We've announced some, you heard about the one on AMRAAM in our prepared remarks, Stinger as well.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We've got strong partnerships with Kongsberg, NASAMS, with MBDA.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So continuing to grow the industrial base there, not only strengthens the relationships, but also continues to add very capable sources to our industrial base and adds capacity and allows us to ramp up to meet that stronger demand internationally.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And when I think about that, about 60% of that step-up is going to come from drop-through on the higher volume that we're going to see across all the channels at Collins in the third and fourth quarter rather.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: They've invested a bit in the first half of this year to begin the realization of those cost reductions, which we expect to start to play through in the second half and then continue out over the next several years.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: And we see no reason why when you think about the growth drivers of that business, more and more out-of-warranty flight hours, a larger installed base, continued ramp on the OE side, really significant and healthy mission systems defense business at Collins as well.

signals.speaker: Neil Mitchill
signals.sentence: All of those things we see growing over the next few years, and that additional volume is going to help with absorption and you couple that with this cost reduction, what you called self-help, and we agree, all of that puts us in a good position to continue to drive these margins higher over the next several years.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And that's going to be a significant part of this margin expansion.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: The Collins team has really taken on in an aggressive way, structural cost reduction actions to drive margin expansion and improve overall profitability and performance.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And again, you know that this is a business that has been created with a number of large acquisitions.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: And this team still is driving a common operational approach to all of these businesses, some of that integration that really hadn't been done yet, all of which we think are going to yield benefits over the next several years.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: I will just tell you that our focus today is on execution, obviously, driving additional deliveries to Airbus supporting the GTF aftermarket and then executing on those 8,000 engines that are still in backlog.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: So we continue to believe that NGSA is going to continue to move to the right because the industry needs stability, our customers want and need stability and supply chain needs and wants stability.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: But to your point, we've been, I think, pretty steadfast in our belief that the next-generation single aisle, especially on the propulsion side, will need to have a different business model.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: I think the idea that we're going to invest all this money upfront and then, again, not have high margins on deliveries and then rely on anywhere from four to six shop visits over a 25-year period.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: I think we need to smooth out some of those cash flows and some of that investment.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: I think all of this, whether it be executing on the backlog we've got today or any of the things that may come into our backlog from the framework agreement is going to be predicated on the supply chain.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: If you look at our year-over-year growth in output, which is really strong, again, a lot of that on the back of these being mature programs, but also the supply chain continuing to step up and deliver at rates.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: As we look to the future, that's going to have to have another significant step up, which is, again, why we're out right now investing in supply chain resiliency.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We're investing in second and third sources in constrained areas.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: They will make the investment.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: But they've got to see that level of visibility and commitment.

signals.speaker: Christopher Calio
signals.sentence: We'll see how the budget ultimately shakes out.
